The generic semaphore rewrite had a huge performance regression on AIM7
(and potentially other BKL-heavy benchmarks) because the generic
semaphores had been rewritten to be simple to understand and fair.  The
latter
column3: turns a semaphore-based BKL implementation into a

column1: mess of scheduling.
The attempt to fix the performance regression failed miserably (see the
previous commit 00b41ec2611dc98f87f30753ee00a53db648d662 'Revert
semaphore: fix""')
column2: and so for now the simple and sane approach is to

column1: instead just go back to the old spinlock-based BKL implementation that
never had any issues like this.
This patch also has the advantage of being reported to fix the
regression completely according to Yanmin Zhang
hack which still left a couple percentage point regression.
As a spinlock
column2: the BKL obviously has the potential to be a latency

column1: issue
column2: but it's not really any different from any other spinlock in that

column1: respect.  We do want to get rid of the BKL asap
plan for several years.
These days
column2: the biggest users are in the tty layer (open/release in

column1: particular) and Alan holds out some hope:
""tty release is probably a few months away from getting cured - I'm
afraid it will almost certainly be the very last user of the BKL in
tty to get fixed as it depends on everything else being sanely locked.""
so while we're not there yet
column2: we do have a plan of action.
